target.title: fix(browser): don't steal focus on headed screenshot captures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Since #100857, `captureScreenshot()` sends `Page.bringToFront` before **every** capture. That guard exists for a headless-specific stall (a backgrounded tab under `--headless=new` never commits a compositor frame, so `Page.captureScreenshot` blocks until the CDP timeout). But on a **headed** browser the same unconditional activation switches the visible tab — and raises the window on some platforms — on every screenshot. Screenshots are the highest-frequency operation in agent browsing loops, so for a headed managed profile (or any browser a human is watching/sharing) the agent constantly steals the user's active tab (#105357).

## Why This Change Was Made

The stall the activation guards against is headless-only, so activation is only needed there. The browser's headed/headless state is already known: for a managed browser (`isLocalManagedProfile`) the resolved profile holds the **authoritative launch flag**, so `captureScreenshot` takes it directly and skips activation only when the browser is confirmed headed.

An earlier revision sniffed `Browser.getVersion`'s `userAgent` for `HeadlessChrome`. That is not robust: a managed headless Chrome can be launched with a custom `--user-agent` (appended via `extraArgs` after `--headless=new` in `chrome.ts`), which a sniff misclassifies as headed — dropping the activation and reintroducing the #100857 stall. The authoritative launch flag now **wins over UA sniffing**, so a custom UA cannot suppress activation.

- **Managed browser** → `headless: profile.headless` (launch flag decides; no `Browser.getVersion` round-trip).
- **Attached/external** session (real state not trustable from config) → `headless: undefined` → best-effort UA sniff fallback, default to activate.

Headless — and any case where detection is unavailable — keeps activating, so the #100857 stall fix is never reintroduced. Explicit focus APIs are unaffected; this only removes the *implicit* per-screenshot focus change. (Companion to #105356, which addresses the same focus hygiene for tab creation.)

## User Impact

- On a headed browser, agent screenshots no longer switch the user's visible tab or raise the window.
- Headless capture behavior is unchanged (tab still activated to force a frame), including headless launched with a custom `--user-agent`.
- One fewer CDP round-trip per screenshot on the common managed path.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — drove the **compiled `captureScreenshot`** against a **real Chrome** over CDP (not the mocked socket). Exact head output:

```
[P1 headless+customUA] headless=true -> PNG=true bytes=2095  (custom non-headless UA did NOT suppress the capture)
[setup] front=A: A.visibility=visible B.visibility=hidden
[P2 headed headless=false] captured B: PNG=true bytes=42044 | A.visibility=visible B.visibility=hidden  -> focus preserved=true
[P3 discriminator headless=true] captured B: PNG=true bytes=42044 | A.visibility=hidden B.visibility=visible  -> focus STOLEN=true
```

- **P1** — real headless Chrome with a custom non-"headless" `--user-agent` (the exact misclassification scenario): `headless=true` capture still returns a valid PNG. No stall.
- **P2** — real headed Chrome, tab A front / B background: capturing B with `headless=false` returns a valid PNG **and** leaves A `visible` / B `hidden` → active tab preserved.
- **P3** — discriminator: the same capture via the activation path (`headless=true`) flips A→`hidden`, B→`visible` → focus genuinely stolen, proving P2 is real behavior, not a mock artifact.

**Regression tests** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.screenshot-params.test.ts` → 15/15):

- `managed headless profile activates even with a custom non-headless UA (#105357)` — launch flag wins over UA; `Page.bringToFront` sent; no `Browser.getVersion`.
- `managed headed profile skips activation even with a headless UA (#105357)` — launch flag wins; `Page.bringToFront` **not** sent.
- `does not steal focus on a headed browser` / `still activates the tab on a headless browser` / `activates when headed detection is unavailable` — external/attached UA-sniff fallback, both directions plus safe default.

**Discriminator**: reverting `cdp.ts` fails the headed tests — the unconditional `Page.bringToFront` returns.

Fixes #105357
